record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Extend renormalization analysis beyond convex Fermi surfaces by treating surfaces with flat pieces and-or singular points, including the half-filled square-lattice Hubbard model.

evidence.quote: Treat non-spherical surfaces. After the work on the renormalization of convex surfaces [FKLT][FST], treat surfaces with flat pieces and/or singular points: the regular Hubbard model at half-filling on a square lattice has both these features.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Develop a rigorous, constructive renormalization-group analysis of two-dimensional interacting many-fermion systems whose Fermi surface is non-convex, in particular possessing flat pieces and/or singular (corner / van Hove) points. Concretely: consider a system of non-relativistic interacting fermions on the square lattice Z^2 with one-particle Hamiltonian given by the standard nearest-neighbor hopping dispersion e(k) = -2t(cos k_1 + cos k_2) (k in the Brillouin zone [-π,π]^2) and on-site Hubbard interaction U n_{x,↑} n_{x,↓}, at chemical potential μ = 0 (half-filling), so that the Fermi surface {k : e(k) = 0} is the square with vertices (±π,0),(0,±π), having both flat sides and corners (van Hove singularities of the density of states). Construct, for U sufficiently small, the thermodynamic and zero-temperature limits of the Schwinger (Green's) functions as convergent power series (or Borel-summable expansions) in U, control the multi-scale renormalization-group flow in the presence of the flat sides and singular corner points, and identify the infrared behavior of the model (e.g. analyticity domain in U, leading low-temperature asymptotics of the two-point function and self-energy, and verification or failure of Fermi-liquid behavior). More generally, extend the sector-decomposition and renormalization methods previously developed for strictly convex C^2 Fermi surfaces in d = 2 to arbitrary Fermi surfaces with flat segments and/or isolated singular points.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial partial progress has been made. Afchain, Magnen, and Rivasseau (Annales Henri Poincaré, 2005) proved analyticity of the half-filled 2D square-lattice Hubbard model in a single RG slice and obtained skeleton-level bounds, controlling the flat-side/van Hove singularity geometry. Benfatto–Giuliani–Mastropietro and Giuliani–Mastropietro extended constructive RG techniques to related non-convex/singular Fermi surfaces (e.g. the honeycomb Hubbard model at half-filling and at van Hove filling). However, a complete construction of the half-filled square-lattice Hubbard model down to zero temperature, and a general renormalization theory for arbitrary Fermi surfaces with flat pieces and singular points, remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: The two dimensional Hubbard Model at half-filling: I. Convergent Contributions
status_evidence.snippet: Analyticity in the coupling constant is proved in a single RG slice for the half-filled 2D Hubbard model.
status_evidence.claim: Partial rigorous renormalization results exist for the half-filled square-lattice Hubbard model.

status_evidence.title: The Hubbard Model at Half-Filling, Part III: Lower Bound on the Self-Energy
status_evidence.snippet: Afchain, Magnen, Rivasseau prove lower bound on the self-energy, indicating non-Fermi-liquid behavior at half-filling.
status_evidence.claim: Progress has been made but the model is not fully constructed.

status_evidence.title: The Two-Dimensional Hubbard Model on the Honeycomb Lattice
status_evidence.snippet: Giuliani–Mastropietro construct the honeycomb Hubbard model at half-filling using constructive RG.
status_evidence.claim: Related non-convex Fermi surface cases have been treated rigorously.

status_evidence.title: Honeycomb Hubbard Model at van Hove Filling
status_evidence.snippet: Recent rigorous constructive RG analysis at van Hove filling on honeycomb lattice.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions to singular Fermi surfaces continue to be active research.
